finding.claim: permitRedirect defaults to true, so a server-supplied redirect_url makes the client open a new connection to an unvalidated host and forward the configured password (and user) there.
finding.source: redirect_url session-state value in OK/handshake packet (lib/cmd/parser.js:169-171, lib/cmd/handshake/authentication.js:100-103), attacker-controlled by a malicious DB server or a plaintext-path MITM.
finding.sink: new Connection(new ConnOptions(Object.assign({}, this.opts, redirectOpts))).connect() at lib/connection.js:1633-1636; this.opts contains password (lib/config/connection-options.js:32).

trace.note: redirect_url from OK packet session tracking
URL parse; scheme must be mariadb:/mysql:
host taken from attacker URL; no allowlist
URL user/password override only if present
original opts (incl. password) merged into redirected connection

finding.guards_checked: Scheme check; same-host skip; no redirect inside transaction; TLS settings inherited so rejectUnauthorized applies; cleartext plugins require TLS (clear-password-auth.js:17, authentication.js:203); caching_sha2/sha256 public-key retrieval opt-in (allowPublicKeyRetrieval). Not guarded: host allowlist, default-on flag, password forwarding when URL has no password. Impact: native_password scramble/response to attacker (offline-crackable) on non-TLS; username always disclosed; SSRF-like connects to internal hosts. Intentional MariaDB feature but on by default.

finding.claim: With permitSetMultiParamEntries enabled, object keys are written inside backticks without escaping, so a key containing a backtick injects arbitrary SQL into the SET clause.
finding.source: Keys of a plain object passed as a ? parameter, e.g. conn.query('UPDATE t SET ? WHERE id=?', [req.body, id]) where req.body keys are attacker-controlled JSON.
finding.sink: out.writeString('`' + key + '`') at lib/cmd/encoder/text-encoder.js:135 (and the escape() equivalent at lib/misc/utils.js:213).

trace.note: branch taken when option enabled and value is a plain object
key concatenated into backtick identifier without escaping

finding.guards_checked: Values are escaped (writeStringEscapeQuote / JSON.stringify path is safe); function-valued props skipped; only keys are unescaped. escapeId (lib/misc/utils.js:91) would double backticks but is not applied to keys. Requires opt-in option plus attacker-controlled keys.
